text:
marta: Seeing a sudden p99 jump from BCN POP over the last 25m, started ~00:05 UTC, affects short-chat routes (<=128 tokens).

sam: Yep noticed it in the dashboards, batching throughput dropped ~30% and CPU sys increased on a few hosts.

marta: root cause looks like a mix of DNS multipath changes at the provider + KV-cache churn. Key symptom: very high connection churn -> lots of tiny batches.

elaine: Can you paste the perf snapshot and the kv stats?

marta: perf top (abridged):
```
Samples:  1K of event 'cycles'
  18.3%  runtime_bin +0x12f  [k] kernel_select_best
  12.1%  runtime_bin +0x7a  [k] emit_batch
   9.0%  libc-2.31.so     [.] __memcmp_sse4_1
   6.4%  runtime_bin       [k] kvcache_lookup
```

marta: KV cache stats from the pop: hit rate dropped 92% -> 64%, evictions spiked. Small-batch rate (<=4) went from 8% -> 46%.

ricardo: That memcmp line suggests a lot of small payload handling and maybe a fallback kernel being chosen repeatedly. Any kernel-selector logs?

marta: Yes. We started seeing kernel-selector flip messages about 00:03 UTC:
```
INFO kernel-selector: candidate=avx512 len=256 cost=8.2ms fallback=avx2
WARN kernel-selector: probe_failed: path-rtt>ms threshold
INFO kernel-selector: switching to fallback=avx2
```

jonathan: Provider change pushed a new DNS multipath policy in BCN at ~00:00. I have traceroutes showing increased path variability and packet reordering. Reordering explains the probe failures -> kernel selector oscillation.

sam: Oscillation + reorders -> lots of small micro-batches because prefixes don't match cached KVs on a consistent host. That will kill throughput and cause memcmp hotspots.

elaine: Any quick mitigations to avoid customer impact?

marta: Mitigation 1: pin kernel selector to prefer-stable (force avx2) on BCN pool to stop oscillation. Mitigation 2: increase kv lookup TTL for small prefixes (reduce evictions). Mitigation 3: temporarily bias batching heuristic to prefer slightly larger batch cutover (min 8) on the short-chat route.

sam: Can we roll a canary config? I can push a per-pop config to one host group.

devops-bot: deploy triggered by sam: deploy_id=deploy-20260318-01, target=bc1-rack[2-3], config_patch=kernel.pin=avx2,batching.min=8,kv.ttl.small=60s

ricardo: After the canary we should collect: kernel-selector logs, kv hit/miss, small-batch ratio, p99 and cpu sys. Also record network metrics (reorder rate, path changes).

marta: Canary up at 00:18 UTC. Initial numbers: p99 down ~22%, small-batch ratio down to 14%, kv hit back to ~88%. CPU sys dropped ~9%.

jonathan: Network team confirmed provider is reverting their multipath policy for BCN region now. They expect stable paths in ~30m.

elaine: Great. Postmortem action items?

marta: Proposed: (1) kernel-selector: add hysteresis to avoid switching on transient probe failures. (2) batching: auto-detect small-batch spike and raise min-batch threshold automatically. (3) kvcache: consider soft-TTL for small-prefix keys during path instability. (4) add network-probe telemetry into the perf dashboard so we correlate reorder/repath events with kernel selection.

sam: +1 on hysteresis. I can prototype a simple cooldown window today.

ricardo: I'll own the postmortem doc and follow-up tasks.

marta: thanks everyone, will keep thread updated if anything else pops up :thumbsup:
